commands.stdout:
PikPak cloud storage command-line tool
Supports file management, folder management, cloud add, and more

Usage:
  pikpak [flags]
  pikpak [command]

Available Commands:
  auth           Authentication management
  completion     Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  config         CLI settings
  cp             Copy file or folder
  download       Download files
  feedback       Feedback to PikPak support
  get            Get file information
  help           Help about any command
  ls             List files and folders
  mcp            Start MCP server for external LLM integration
  mkdir          Create folder
  mv             Move file or folder
  play           Play media file
  rename         Rename file or folder
  rm             Move files or folders to the recycle bin
  share          Share management
  skill          Install the PikPak skill into your AI coding agents
  star           Star a file
  task           Task management
  trash          Browse the recycle bin and restore files
  unstar         Unstar a file
  update         Update pikpak to the latest version
  upload         Upload a file or directory
  version        Display version information

Flags:
  -F, --format string   Output format: json, yaml (default: human-readable)
  -h, --help            help for pikpak
  -v, --verbose         Enable verbose output
      --version         Show version

Use "pikpak [command] --help" for more information about a command.

List contents of a directory. Use --type=file or --type=folder to filter

Usage:
  pikpak ls [folderID] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help            help for ls
  -l, --limit int       Items per page (default 100)
  -p, --parent string   Parent folder ID
      --raw             Return the unmodified PikPak API JSON (structured output; -F yaml converts it)
  -t, --token string    Page token
      --type string     Filter type: file or folder

Global Flags:
  -F, --format string   Output format: json, yaml (default: human-readable)
  -v, --verbose         Enable verbose output
      --version         Show version

Get detailed file information.
By default returns basic info. Use --url-type to return URLs (download, play, or all).
Use --raw to return the API response unchanged, including fields the typed output drops (params, medias, apps, audit).

Usage:
  pikpak get <fileID> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help              help for get
      --raw               Return the unmodified PikPak API JSON (structured output; -F yaml converts it)
      --url-type string   URL type: download, play, or all

Global Flags:
  -F, --format string   Output format: json, yaml (default: human-readable)
  -v, --verbose         Enable verbose output
      --version         Show version

Show whether you are logged in and, if so, the active account's profile, VIP membership and storage quota.

Usage:
  pikpak auth status [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for status

Global Flags:
  -F, --format string   Output format: json, yaml (default: human-readable)
  -v, --verbose         Enable verbose output
      --version         Show version

Login to PikPak account via Web or Device authorization

Usage:
  pikpak auth login [flags]

Flags:
      --continue string     Poll device code status once and exit (use with -F json)
      --force               Create a new session even if already logged in
  -h, --help                help for login
  -l, --label string        Session label (default: hostname · parent_process)
  -m, --method string       Login method: 'device' or 'browser' (auto-detect if unset)
      --no-launch-browser   Don't open browser automatically (manual mode)
      --scope string        Pre-select OAuth scopes (comma-separated API identifiers)

Global Flags:
  -F, --format string   Output format: json, yaml (default: human-readable)
  -v, --verbose         Enable verbose output
      --version         Show version

commands.stdout:
Download one or more files from PikPak cloud storage to the local filesystem.
Use -o to specify the output path (single file only), or files are saved with their
original names in the current directory.
Use --url-only to only print the download URL without downloading.

Usage:
  pikpak download <fileID> [fileID...] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help            help for download
  -o, --output string   Output file path
      --parallel int    Connections per file, 1-8 (files at least 16MB are split into ranges) (default 8)
      --url-only        Print the download URL instead of downloading

Global Flags:
  -F, --format string   Output format: json, yaml (default: human-readable)
  -v, --verbose         Enable verbose output
      --version         Show version
